clue.text: Higher return from industry?

parts.note: a bigger reward from one's work, read as what a worker gets in wages, while 'industry' poses as a sector of the economy

explanation.surface: An economist wonders whether manufacturing yields better profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return from industry' looks like profit on investment; read 'industry' as hard work and the higher return is what an employee earns for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in wages is a larger reward for one's labour.

clue.text: A plant forming part of our nuclear umbrella

indicators.note: forming part of says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A defence commentator speaks of something planted within the nuclear deterrent.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a well-known flowering species of the genus Arum.

clue.text: Mean old boy Nigel cunningly -gets round

indicators.note: gets round means the shuffled name surrounds the other piece
done cunningly, the letters of the name are artfully rearranged

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A crafty man named Nigel dodges the rules and is thought base for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like average or stingy here; it is the adjective for base. 'cunningly' shuffles the name and 'gets round' wraps it around the old-boy abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble describes base, dishonourable conduct, as does mean in its sense of petty.

clue.text: Comb one might get for Christmas

definitions.meaning: to comb wool or fibres before spinning is to ... them
a greeting sent through the post at the festive season

explanation.definitionFit: Carding is the textile process of combing fibres, and a greetings piece of folded stiff paper arrives at Christmas.

clue.text: Fleet Street VIPs sorted out

parts.note: the senior newspaper people who correct and arrange copy, read as the people who sort it out

explanation.surface: Important press figures have their problems settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the home of the British national newspapers; the senior staff there put copy in order, which is the sorting out.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper chiefs who prepare and correct copy for print are its editors.

clue.text: Boorish fellow makes 50 cry out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the word for cry is placed around the number

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An uncouth man reduces fifty people to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is read as outside: SOB sits around L, giving S-L-OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A slob is a lazy, uncouth and slovenly person.

clue.text: Frugal life style to which -flat-dwellers are accustomed?

definitions.meaning: a simple, thrifty way of existing without luxuries
people who dwell on flat land, prairie or plains folk, live in that terrain

explanation.definitionFit: Plain living means a modest, thrifty existence, and plains dwellers literally live on the level ground.

clue.text: Shameful way to sell one's land

definitions.text: Shameful way to sell one's land

parts.words: Shameful way to sell one's land
parts.note: selling out one's country, read as if it were a property sale

explanation.surface: Someone disposes of their estate in a disgraceful manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sell one's land' looks like a property deal; it means betraying one's country.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray one's country to an enemy is to become a traitor.

clue.text: What Parliament is when discussing business?

definitions.meaning: a scornful label for an assembly that debates but does nothing
a store where trade is being talked over, a shop in conversation

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a disparaging name for a debating body, and literally a shop where people are chatting.

clue.text: Religious work prominently featured in the Sunday tabloids.

definitions.meaning: the final book of the New Testament

definitions.text: prominently featured in the Sunday tabloids.
definitions.meaning: exposés and scandalous disclosures splashed across weekend papers

explanation.definitionFit: The Book of the Apocalypse is a biblical text, and sensational disclosures are the stuff of popular weekend papers.

clue.text: Foxhounds, for instance, treated, as beasts of burden

definitions.meaning: hunting dogs that run together in a group
mules or donkeys that carry loads

explanation.definitionFit: Hounds hunt as a group, and load-carrying mules and llamas carry packs.

clue.text: Irish boy bringing the post round

indicators.note: brought round, the word for the post is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A young Irish lad delivers letters on his route.
explanation.definitionFit: Liam is a common Irish male first name, a short form of William.

clue.text: Off-beat classical character

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unconventional figure from ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, a character of a classical language.

clue.text: Article the scribe had to dip into

definitions.text: Article the scribe had to dip into

parts.words: Article the scribe had to dip into
parts.note: the desk container a writer with a pen repeatedly dipped into for colour

explanation.surface: A copyist was obliged to consult some piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of writing and 'dip into' suggests reading; it is an object a pen is dipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Before fountain pens, writers dipped their nibs into a pot of ink set in the desk.

clue.text: Painful result of craning to see a woodpecker?

definitions.text: Painful result of craning to see
definitions.meaning: a stiff twisted neck from stretching to look
a small bird of the woodpecker family that twists its head

explanation.definitionFit: A wry neck is a crick from twisting, and the wryneck is a bird related to woodpeckers.

clue.text: Currency they had at Hamelin

parts.note: currency read as current, a flowing river, at the German town of the Pied Piper

explanation.surface: A question about what money was used in the Pied Piper's town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currency' is read as something with a current, a river; Hamelin stands on the Weser in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The German river that runs through Hamelin carries a current.

clue.text: Superior housing projections

parts.note: parts of a roof that jut out above the walls of a house

explanation.surface: Estate agents forecast better homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projections' looks like forecasts and 'superior housing' like upmarket homes; they are overhangs on top of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower edges of a roof overhang the walls high on a building.

clue.text: An old torch connection

definitions.meaning: a flaming torch once carried to light the streets
a tie or bond between things

explanation.definitionFit: Linkboys once carried pitch torches for hire, and a chain's ring joins one piece to the next.

clue.text: A point about suffering

indicators.note: about means the word for point is placed around the A

parts.note: a pin has a point and can stand for one

explanation.surface: Someone notes a particular aspect of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is physical or mental distress, the condition of one who suffers.

clue.text: Sat in the studio and propounded a question

definitions.meaning: sat as a model for an artist or photographer
put forward a problem for consideration

explanation.definitionFit: An artist's model holds a pose, and one puts a question to a meeting.

clue.text: Pillage distributed in a popular part of Paris

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread about into a new order

explanation.surface: Plunder is shared out in a busy district of the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigalle is a Paris district known for its nightlife and Moulin Rouge.

clue.text: Settle for the account that attracts interest

definitions.meaning: to settle as sediment, laying down a layer
a bank account earning interest on savings

explanation.definitionFit: Silt is laid down when it settles, and a bank's savings account pays interest.

clue.text: Face to face with about six passport endorsements?

indicators.note: about means the word for passport stamps goes around the number

parts.note: visas are stamps endorsing a passport
VI is the Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Travel stamps confront someone at a border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you the plural of the passport word goes round the Roman six, which lands just before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means opposite or in relation to, literally one person facing another.

clue.text: Sticking to the facts about Islam's transformation

parts.note: RE is Latin for about, concerning

indicators.note: a transformation changes form, so the letters of the faith's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scholar writes on how a religion has changed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Latin for 'in the matter of', is a crossword staple for about; 'transformation' rearranges the faith's name after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is a practical, factual outlook rather than an idealistic one.

clue.text: Secluded place that's negative all right?

explanation.surface: A hidden spot is described as unsatisfactory yet fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or hidden recess.

clue.text: Turbid lake that is green in colour

indicators.note: turbid water is stirred up and muddy, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddy lake looks green.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a leafy cabbage, and greens are leafy vegetables.

clue.text: A cliff that doesn't improve the landscape?

definitions.meaning: a steep rocky crag on a hillside
a blemish or ugly mark on land, like a wound mark on skin

explanation.definitionFit: A crag is called this in northern England, and a disfiguring mark spoils a view as a wound mark spoils skin.

clue.text: Motherless animal that turns blue?

indicators.note: less means without, so letters are taken away from the creature

parts.note: MA is a word for mother

explanation.surface: An orphaned creature becomes sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motherless' looks like orphaned; it means the creature less MA. Anil is the indigo plant, whose dye colours things blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The anil shrub yields indigo, a dye that colours cloth deep blue.

clue.text: Further from Laos

indicators.note: made from suggests the letters of the country are reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: Somewhere more distant than a South-East Asian country.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and further both mean in addition, besides.

clue.text: Highly skilled Spanish bow man

parts.note: a virtuoso Catalan cellist, whose bow is a cello bow rather than an archer's

explanation.surface: An expert Spanish archer is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow man' suggests an archer; it is a player who uses a bow on strings, the great Catalan cellist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan virtuoso was one of the twentieth century's greatest cellists.

clue.text: Amazingly considerate act of profanity

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters of the word are thrown into astonishing disorder

explanation.surface: Someone does something surprisingly thoughtful while being profane.
explanation.definitionFit: Desecration is violating something sacred, an irreverent act.
